findings.classification: Newly assessed conditional native source contract mismatch; no demonstrated product reachability or accepted duplicate count
trace: tiny-skia pixmap.rs:238–243 and 348–353 promise None for an out-of-bounds position but compute width*y+x and only bounds-check the resulting one-dimensional pixel slice. For a 2×2 exact-length pixmap, x=2,y=0 forms index2, which lies within the four-element slice and addresses the next row even though x is out of width. The checked arithmetic prevents overflow but does not check each coordinate.

Pixmap::from_vec validates exact buffer length at 56–68; tiny-skia-path size.rs:13–30 and lib.rs:62–63 admit nonzero 2×2 dimensions. PixmapRef uses the same formula; its permissive borrowed-buffer extent at pixmap.rs:293–306 can also expose trailing complete pixels for out-of-height coordinates.

findings.classification: Newly assessed conditional native admission/operation mismatch; no demonstrated product reachability or accepted count
trace: pixmap.rs:293–306 and 451–465 explicitly accept a byte slice whose length is at least the minimum and retain the full slice. pixmap.rs:356–358 and 518–520 cast the full slice to PremultipliedColorU8, a transparent [u8;4] type (tiny-skia color.rs:91–100).

For a 1×1 size, four bytes are required; an otherwise valid five-byte borrowed slice passes the length check, yet is not divisible into four-byte pixels. Locked bytemuck 1.25.2 lib.rs:405–429,496–515 and internal.rs:247–272,353–373,381–405 reject slop and cast_slice/cast_slice_mut panic on error. Thus a subsequent pixels()/pixels_mut(), and PixmapMut::fill which calls pixels_mut at pixmap.rs:503–507, can panic rather than work on the admitted four-byte image region.

With a larger excess divisible by four, pixmap.rs:312–316,356–358 and 503–507 instead expose/copy/mutate the whole slice, including bytes beyond the declared image extent; exact desired handling of an oversized borrowed slice is the documented at-least contract to reconcile.
findings.conditions: The stated sizes are mathematical reasoning, not a generated input or executed image. Requires a supported caller to supply an oversized borrowed buffer and access the related operations. Current studio uses the exact-length owned Pixmap::from_vec and does not prove this route. All direct/indirect consumers and native package policies remain open.
